summary: Two messages in fourteen days, both ALTR-side, both internal, both on the same afternoon — and between them they say this client is gone. On 2026-09-05 Stephski wrote in the DMCA topic '@sotom225 shes not with us anymore' and Michelle ([REDACTED-RECOVERY-EMAIL]) replied 'yes we removed already'. That is the entire window. Nobody has addressed Cheyene herself since Stephski's payment chase on 2026-08-26 — 16 days ago. Cheyene has not written a word since 2026-08-11 — 31 days ago. The last genuine two-way exchange of any kind was the Aug 11 payment thread where she asked for four more days; the last two-way exchange about actual service was 2026-07-23, 50 days ago, when Mayson checked her account status and told her 'Looks all good'. Three corroborating signals confirm the offboarding is real and not a misread: Michelle's weekly leak-removal breakdown ran Aug 10, Aug 17 and Aug 25 and then stopped dead — nothing on Sep 1 or Sep 8; the Aug 15-31 invoice that was due to go out on 2026-09-01 was never sent, so billing stopped too; and no ALTR message of any kind has been directed at the client in 16 days. This account was not lost this window — it was lost weeks ago and only recorded this window, in a two-line side conversation between two staff members, in a topic the client can read. Two invoices are still unpaid and were never resolved before the removal: the July 15-31 invoice, 41 days from send and 34 days past its Aug 8 due date, and the combined Aug 15 bill (July balance plus Aug 1-14, the largest of the relationship), 27 days from send and 20 days past its implied Aug 22 due date. No termination message was ever sent to her, no final statement, no collections handoff, and no answer to the question of whether she stopped paying because she could not pay or because she never acknowledged the bank account number that changed on Aug 15 — 27 days unverified and now probably unverifiable. Every prior week's headline recommendation, above all 'phone or SMS her on [REDACTED-NUMBER]', went unactioned right up to the removal.

This is no longer a distressed account, it is a closed one: ALTR staff stated internally on 2026-09-05 that the client 'is not with us anymore' and confirmed she had already been removed from the service. Service delivery has stopped (leak-removal reports ended Aug 25, 17 days), billing has stopped (the Sep 1 invoice was never sent), and client-facing communication has stopped (16 days since anyone spoke to her, 31 days since she spoke to us). It is not zero for two reasons only: the departure was never formally communicated to the client, so a reversal is technically still possible if someone reaches her; and two unpaid invoices remain live, meaning there is still money on the table and therefore still a reason to act. Nothing in this window was a recovery attempt.

Close this slug out in the weekly run. With no service, no billing and no client-facing contact, continuing to score it every week produces noise. Carry it as a receivable and a post-mortem, not as a live account, unless contact is re-established.
